column3: Exact parallel of mutual أولياء among a ظلم-marked bloc; also frames affiliation as consequential.
Supplies the تقوى pole, but adds no relation of ولاية or failed sufficiency.
Directly names mutual attachment among الظالمين and ties it to their earning.
Near-verbatim parallel: a contrary group is بعضهم أولياء بعض, clarifying bloc formation.
Associates faith and تقوى with rescue, a secondary outcome for the protected side.
Its negation of تقوى characterizes covenant-breaking, but not the support contrast itself.
Eschatological reversal of close mutual relations, with المتقين as the stated exception.
Mercy is the stated exception to failed intercession; it bounds the no-avail claim.
Self-protection and household responsibility extend the protective dimension of تقوى.
Direct parallel to لن يغنوا من الله شيئا, specifying wealth and children as inadequate.
Shows the protected destination of المتقين, though it does not name ولاية.
The occurrence of بعض concerns sayings, not mutual support, protection, or sufficiency.
Positive counterpart: believers become mutual أولياء through aid and entrusted security.
Allah as ولي at the moment of faltering concretizes reliable protection.
A reminder for المتقين contributes only the shared piety designation.
Positive mutual ولاية is defined by communal obedience, contrasting the wrongdoers' bloc.
Mutual enmity supplies a contrary social relation, without the support or sufficiency claim.
Explicitly contrasts Allah as مولى of believers with the absence of any مولى for disbelievers.
يغنوا here concerns former dwelling, not inability to avail before Allah.
False gods fail to avail at divine judgment, directly expanding failed recourse.
Immediate same-surah parallel joins failed availing with taken أولياء besides Allah.
Treaty fidelity and divine love of المتقين provide only a peripheral ethical condition.
Reliance on the Lord marks a protected party beyond satanic authority.
Direct eschatological parallel: no مولى avails another and no help arrives.
Negated harm to Allah and punishment do not develop the verse's relation of support.
Shows harmful authority through taking a patron, a secondary contrary patronage pattern.
Explicit Allah مولى provides the reliable-protector side, despite a different local setting.
Kin and children cannot benefit at judgment, a secondary limit on social support.
Regulates taking contrary أولياء and preserves the allegiance boundary, though context is narrower.
The contrast route marks a boundary only; turning away alone adds no support relation.
Mutual non-following and ظلم are a distant parallel to divided affiliation.
Reward for belief and righteous action adds only general positive context.
Negated sufficiency is confined to shade against flame and is not the divine-relational claim.
Removing a burden lacks the candidate verse's network or sufficiency structure.
Garden reward for المتقين reinforces the protected outcome already established.
A warning involving the opposite group and تقوى is too general after earlier cards.
يغنوا again describes prior habitation rather than failed defense or substitution.
Peer calling is unrelated to mutual guardianship or inability to avail.
Concise declaration that Allah is مولى and the best helper states the positive pole.
Former dwelling and loss do not clarify the support contrast.
No protection from Allah and punishment are relevant but do not specify the mutual bloc.
The contrast route is boundary evidence only; the battle response adds no exact relation.
No ولي after Allah, joined to الظالمين facing punishment, closely supports the boundary.
The admonition to glorify supplies no direct relation of تقوى, ولاية, or sufficiency.
Allah's self-sufficiency is a broad asymmetry, not a claim about human failed support.
Covenant fulfillment and تقوى give a secondary profile of the protected group.
Routine household circulation among people is not an alliance or protective relation.
Allah as مولى and نصير explicitly supplies the effective-protector alternative.
Being among المتقين is retrospective and does not develop protection or alliance.
Continues the aided-believer formation from 8:72 and supplies its positive outcome.
The call to تقوى and mercy is broad secondary support only.
Allah as ولي of believers provides the positive guardianship identity.
Prayer for protection from fire is a limited protective echo without the relation contrast.
Contrasts sinful secret cooperation with righteousness and تقوى, preserving a secondary network reading.
Taking devils as أولياء apart from Allah gives a concrete contrary-patronage pattern.
Turning away and divine dislike lack a distinct support or sufficiency contribution.
Self-sufficiency in the negative path gives a secondary contrast to dependence on Allah.
Garden reward for المتقين repeats the protected outcome with little new route detail.
A divided culpable group is only a distant social parallel.
Wealth cannot avail at ruin, a direct but already well-covered insufficiency instance.
The prophetic disclaimer does not add mutual support, patronage, or failed availing.
Witness and knowledge of the Book are outside the candidate relation.
Near-duplicate of 58:17: wealth and children cannot avail from Allah.
Absence of any ولي or helper from Allah gives the boundary, though framed by following desires.
Following Allah's messenger and love does not independently specify the protection contrast.
Allah's being with المتقين reinforces divine proximity, in a specialized setting.
Mutual wrongdoing among associates is a loose analogue to the wrongdoers' mutuality.
Hypocrites are described as mutually belonging and organized around shared wrongdoing.
The repeated formula that conjecture cannot avail against truth broadens the insufficiency principle.
Invoked objects are powerless, supporting the failure of alternatives to divine adequacy.
Mutual blame after failure is a faint downstream contrast to mutual protective alliance.
Turning away alone is only contrast-boundary material and lacks the focal relation.
No ولي or نصير besides Allah supplies a broad, explicit protection boundary.
Historical self-wronging supports the ظلم category but adds no relation of ولاية.
Giving with تقوى contrasts the self-sufficient path, but remains generic after earlier evidence.
Divine aid is relevant as outcome but has no patronage or mutuality detail.
No ولي or protector from Allah under following desires restates the exclusive boundary.
The divided-piece wording has no connection to alliance, piety, or failed sufficiency.
Discernment of truthful and false claimants does not develop the focal contrast.
Submission or turning away here supplies no specific support or guardianship relation.
The contrast route is boundary evidence only; corruption adds no exact support claim.
Those who turn away have no ولي or helper, a secondary exclusive-protection boundary.
Turning away from judgment is not an affiliation or sufficiency parallel.
Explicit command to تقوى reinforces the protected identity but adds no new mechanism.
Directly says a worshiped alternative cannot avail anything, a key false-recourse parallel.
Satisfaction with effort does not bear on the candidate's support contrast.
Cooperation on righteousness and تقوى is a broad ethical counterpart; the contrast route is only boundary evidence.
Foundation on تقوى versus a collapsing wrongful foundation gives an indirect structural contrast.
Accounting alone supplies no support, piety, or failed-substitution relation.
Worldly enjoyment cannot avail, extending the insufficiency motif without the Allah boundary.
Mutual trust plus تقوى is a narrow transactional relation, not guardianship.
Human neediness before Allah gives the dependence side of the no-avail asymmetry.
Exclusive worship and a piety question offer only a broad anti-alternative boundary.
The command to تقوى and obedience is generic and adds no relation mechanism.
Guidance and misguidance here do not specify alliance, protection, or sufficiency.
The occurrence of بعض is distributive property, unrelated to mutual support.
Shared inheritance portions are unrelated to the candidate's moral and protective relations.
The call to worship and تقوى is a generic background marker only.
Avoiding idols is a broad boundary against alternatives, without the focal support claim.
Faculties and resources cannot avail their possessors, a strong expanded insufficiency example.
No person can suffice for another before Allah, directly reinforcing the failure of substitute support.
Denies any ولي or نصير apart from Allah, stating the exclusive-protection boundary.
A second direct no-soul-avails formulation, with no ransom or intercession accepted.
Allah's ولاية for believers versus false-patron ولاية for disbelievers gives the core two-sided contrast.
The prayer names Allah as مولى and seeks aid, supplying the positive dependence response.
Wealth and children will not avail from Allah, an exact close parallel to 45:19.
If Allah withholds help, no one can help; this fixes effective aid in divine protection.
Allah's sufficiency is stated as the believers' reliance, a compact positive counterpart.
Allah is explicitly sufficient as ولي and نصير, directly naming the effective alternative.
The oppressed ask Allah for a ولي and نصير, specifying the protective need of the exposed.
Forbids taking the contrary party as أولياء, preserving the allegiance boundary.
Taking Satan as ولي identifies a ruinous alternative patronage relation.
No ولي or نصير is available apart from Allah, a direct protection boundary.
Taking disbelievers as أولياء apart from believers develops the wrongful allegiance pattern.
Direct prohibition on taking disbelievers as أولياء apart from believers.
Defines the positive ولي relation through Allah, the messenger, and believing worshippers.
Forbids taking hostile religious mockers as أولياء, a contextual allegiance boundary.
Condemns taking disbelievers as أولياء, supplying another wrongful-bloc instance.
Allah is named ولي as creator and sustainer, supporting the exclusive protector pole.
Those gathered before their Lord have no ولي or intercessor apart from Him.
Denies any ولي or intercessor besides Allah and rejects compensating substitutes.
Devils inspire their أولياء, extending the contrary network beyond human mutuality.
Allah is their ولي because of their deeds, joining protected status to faithful conduct.
Forbids following أولياء besides Allah, an explicit exclusive-allegiance boundary.
Devils are أولياء of those without faith, a contrary patronage relation.
Allah is the ولي of the righteous, closely matching Allah's ولاية of the pious.
Even kin are not to be taken as أولياء when they prefer disbelief, testing social allegiance.
No ولي or نصير exists apart from Allah, a concise exclusive-protection statement.
Allah's أولياء are marked by security rather than fear or grief, expanding the protected side.
Denies any أولياء besides Allah to those unable to escape divine judgment.
Forbids inclination toward الظالمين and warns that no أولياء then remain besides Allah.
يوسف names Allah as ولي in worldly life and the hereafter, an explicit durable guardianship claim.
Challenges taking أولياء besides Allah that control neither benefit nor harm.
Satan is identified as the ولي of a misguided people, a contrary patronage pattern.
Whoever Allah leaves astray has no ولي besides Him, directly marking exclusive guidance and protection.
Allah has no ولي from weakness, sharply excluding any need for supporting patronage.
No ولي مرشد is found for one Allah leaves astray, a guidance-protection boundary.
ولاية is declared to belong to Allah, the True, making divine guardianship the governing frame.
Fear of becoming Satan's ولي supplies a personal contrary-patronage outcome.
Calls the false patron an evil مولى and companion, directly evaluating alternative protection.
Denies any ولي or نصير apart from Allah to those unable to thwart Him.
Those taking أولياء besides Allah are portrayed as relying on a structurally inadequate refuge.
Neither parent nor child can avail the other, a close interpersonal parallel to 45:19.
No ولي or intercessor exists besides Allah, directly joining guardianship and failed mediation.
No one can protect from Allah or secure mercy against His will.
The condemned find neither ولي nor نصير, an eschatological counterpart to failed support.
Other gods are taken in hope of aid, directly exposing a failed alternative-support structure.
Those taking أولياء besides Allah state their rationale, directly presenting the rival-allegiance claim.
No invoked alternative can remove Allah's harm or withhold His mercy, testing claimed protection.
The ظالمون have neither devoted ally nor an obeyed intercessor at judgment.
A declared worldly-and-hereafter ولاية supplies a positive, durable protection counterpart.
Allah watches those who take أولياء besides Him, preserving the rival-allegiance boundary.
After questioning rival أولياء, the verse declares Allah alone is ولي and life-giver.
Those wronging themselves have no أولياء to help them besides Allah.
Calling what cannot answer apart from Allah expands the inadequacy of alternative recourse.
The gods taken as means of nearness fail to help, directly exemplifying failed substitute support.
No ransom is accepted and no مولى remains, an eschatological failure of all substitute recourse.
Forbids taking Allah's enemies and one's enemies as أولياء, a direct allegiance boundary.
Reliance on Allah is answered by His sufficiency, giving the positive dependence mechanism.
No one can protect from Allah and no ملتحد is found besides Him.
After Allah's decree, people have no ولي besides Him, extending the exclusive-protection boundary.
What is worshiped besides Allah lacks provision and power, a secondary alternative-inadequacy parallel.
Invoked alternatives cannot remove or redirect harm, directly testing their claimed protective force.
The question of who guards people from the Merciful frames protection as exclusively divine.
Questioning worship of what neither benefits nor harms challenges alternative recourse.
Allah protects while none can protect against Him, directly defining asymmetrical effective defense.
False gods possess neither benefit nor harm, life nor death, exposing their incapacity as alternatives.
Provision is to be sought from Allah rather than false objects, a dependence-side parallel.
Those invoked besides Allah possess nothing, extending the incapacity of alternative supports.
No one can withhold Allah's mercy or release what He withholds, reinforcing exclusive efficacy.
False intercession cannot avail or save against divine harm, a close failed-recourse parallel.
Allah's sufficiency for His servant states the positive answer to failed reliance on others.
Those called besides Allah lack intercession authority except by true knowledge, bounding substitute mediation.
No one can protect disbelievers from painful punishment, directly restating failed protection from Allah.
The messenger disclaims power over harm and guidance, a limited witness to creaturely insufficiency.
